data.name: Chain_Title
data.value: How a chain works

data.name: Chain_Intro
data.value:
ChainRenamer renames files with a **chain** of small steps. Each step does one simple thing (sort, replace a text…) and works on the result of the step above it, like an assembly line.
The first step is always the **Source**: the folder and the files to rename. Add the next steps with **+ Add a module**; the same module can be used several times. Drag a step by its handle ≡ to change the order: the result changes with it, since each step starts from what the previous one produced.
**Click a step to see what it does.** The grid then shows each name before and after this step, and the names it changes are highlighted. The last step shows the final names. A rule that goes wrong is spotted at once, at the step where it happens.
**Nothing touches the disk** until you click **Apply renaming**. Until then, try anything.
A step can be switched off: it then passes its input on unchanged, which lets you compare with and without it. A step whose settings are not valid (a regular expression being typed, for instance) is marked ⚠ and also passes its input on.
Give a step a name (“Dots to spaces”) to find your way in a long chain: it is shown under its module in the chain.

data.name: Selection_Title
data.value: Check boxes and selection

data.name: Selection_Intro
data.value:
The first column of the grid holds check boxes. They mean two different things, depending on the selected step:
• In the **Source** step, a file left unchecked is **out of the whole chain**. No step sees it, and it is never renamed. • In a step that changes names (Replace…), a file left unchecked is **skipped by this step only**. The step leaves its name as it is, shown in grey italics, and the other steps still work on it. Handy when a rule suits every file but a few.
A Sort step has no check boxes: its column holds the handles ≡ that move the files by hand.
**Fast selection** • The check box in the header checks or unchecks every file. • Shift + click on a check box: the whole range since the last one clicked. • Press on a row and drag: a rectangle selects the rows, as in the Explorer. With Ctrl, they are added to the selection. • Space checks or unchecks the selected rows. A right click offers check, uncheck and invert.

Library_Title
data.value: Saved chains and favorites

data.name: Library_Intro
data.value:
A chain is a recipe: **File > Save** keeps its steps and their settings in the library, to replay them later on another folder. The source folder is not saved with it: load the folder, then open the chain from the **Chains** menu.
• **Save** (Ctrl+S) replaces the open chain. **Save as…** (Ctrl+Shift+S) makes a new one, to start from an existing chain. The name is typed in the top bar. • A **•** in the window title means changes not saved yet. Opening another chain or closing the window asks first. • The files unchecked in a step and an order set by hand depend on the loaded files: they are not saved.
**Favorites**, as in a browser: **Chains > In favorites** (Ctrl+D) puts the open chain at the top of the Chains menu. **Organize favorites…** sorts them into folders, which become submenus (Series ▸ Anime). A favorite is only a shortcut: removing it never deletes the chain.
**The library** is a folder holding one `.chain` file per chain, by default `%APPDATA%\ChainRenamer\chains`. **Change the library location…** moves it, to a NAS or a synced folder for example: your chains then follow you from one PC to another.
**Import and export.** **Export this chain…** makes a file to send to someone. **Export the whole library…** makes a zip, for a backup or a new PC. **Import…** takes `.chain` files and these zips; a name already taken gets a number: “Series (2)”.

data.name: Source_Intro
data.value:
The fixed first step: it chooses the files to rename. It cannot be moved nor removed.
Type a folder or click **Browse…**, then **Load**. Local folders and network shares both work, and a slow network does not freeze the window.
Then uncheck the files to leave out: they leave the whole chain (see “Check boxes and selection”). The folder is not saved with the chain: a chain can be replayed on any folder.

data.name: Source_Folder_Text
data.value: A local folder (`D:\Videos`) or a network share (`\\nas\video\Series`).

data.name: Source_Subfolders_Text
data.value: Also lists the files of every subfolder. Each file stays in its own folder when it is renamed.

data.name: Sort_Intro
data.value:
Puts the files in order. The order matters for the modules that number the files or give them the lines of a list: the first file gets number 1, or the first line.
**Natural order**: the numbers in the names are compared as numbers, so `Episode 2` comes before `Episode 10`. A plain alphabetical sort would put `Episode 10` first.
**By hand**: drag a file by its handle ≡ in the grid. The order set by hand lasts as long as the files stay loaded; it is not saved with the chain. **Back to natural order** cancels it.

data.name: Sort_Descending_Text
data.value: From the last to the first: Z to A, 10 to 1.

data.value: Natural order: 2 before 10

data.name: Replace_Intro
data.value:
Replaces a text by another in the name. The text is searched exactly as it is typed: `.` is a dot. To find a pattern (any number, any word…), use **Replace (advanced)**.
The extension is never touched: replacing `.` by a space keeps `.mkv`.

data.name: Regex_Intro
data.value:
Replaces what a **regular expression** finds: a pattern rather than a fixed text. Parentheses capture parts of the name, which the replacement puts back with `$1`, `$2`…, in any order.
Like Replace, it never touches the extension. While a pattern is being typed and is not valid yet, the step is marked ⚠ and changes nothing.

data.name: Regex_Pattern_Text
Regex_With_Text
data.value: The new text. `$1` puts back the first group, `$2` the second… Empty, it deletes what the pattern finds.

data.name: Regex_MatchCase_Text
data.value: Checked, `[a-z]` finds lowercase letters only. Unchecked, case is ignored.

data.name: Regex_Example_Season
data.value: `(\d+)x(\d+)` by `S$1E$2`: season and episode

data.name: Regex_Example_Swap
data.value: `^(.+) - (.+)$` by `$2 - $1`: swaps the two parts

data.name: Regex_Example_Brackets
data.value: `\s*\[.*?\]` by nothing: removes what is between brackets

data.name: Regex_Example_Spaces
data.value: `\s+` by a space: several spaces become one
